"Friends of all appearances, if I may add add to the discussion with my experiences. My name is Roy Gat Bivur - that is, given name Roy, of the Gat family, from the Bivur swarm. I'm a swarmkeeper from the old world, from the communities living together with colonies of insects."

"Where I'm from, among the communities of the greater swarm, here's how things work: each community is mostly self-governing, and its common insect colony is a slightly different variant of the greater swarm, more fitting for their environment. Each community sends representants to the gatherings where matters affecting all communities are discussed. Now, would I speak in favor of using exactly the same for Arcania? No."

"The problem with it was that eventually it regressed to several families calling the shots, regardless of whether they're fit for it. And the Gat family has been one of such. Which is why I was sent across the ocean to start seeking means of refuge for the greater swarm in case the wars consume our communities. Not because I was the best for the task - because my family wanted to make sure my brother's the one to take over after them, and keep things the way they've been."

"What I'm saying is, there is value in doing things that way - who'll know better what let's say one community needs, people from it, or ones from a completely different environment? But at the same time, this is delicate balance that requires care. While I agree with the points you've been making so far, I want to point to what our friend Bones has been saying as source of wisdom, and caution."

"While I agree that we need the best among us to lead, I don't believe merit equals merit - I don't think I'd trust someone like myself to be in charge of, say, health of the citizens. But, at the same time, those closest to the common folk, working hard for themselves, their families, and communities, should definitely have their voice heard and considered, maybe even followed."

"With that context, to what you've been discussing, I'd like to suggest the following: no leaders should be all-powerful, because no mortal person can know everything. Let us have someone that would coordinate everything, yes, but accompanied by those best in their field to provide everything one needs to make decisions. Example, let's say, about teachers. One to be in charge of schooling would have to have experience in it. One who has never experienced it from both the student and teacher perspective, shouldn't decide on things that don't affect them."

"But, this too would need careful tending to, of course. Following just that, we'd eventually go back to square one, with only the old and established deciding, and influencing anyone new to follow the exact same path. No progress, only past. So I suggest that each body in charge of a specific area has both the experienced and established, and those currently affected by it. No one or two or three people can ever have a complete picture. Swarms, machines, and communities are all alike. There might be one central part making decisions like ones you're discussing, but these decisions come based on what other parts experience. Does that make sense?"
